formats.key: createOperator(address _owner, string _name, uint256 _operatorFee, uint256 _maximumOperatorFee, address[] _recipients, uint256[] _percents)
effects: Only the factory owner can call it (onlyOwner); it spends no assets of the signer.
Deploys a new Operator contract owned by _owner (Ownable2Step) with the given name.
Sets the operator fee in bps (must be <= maximum fee) and an immutable maximum fee in bps (<= 10000).
Sets the commission recipients and their bps shares (sorted, non-zero, summing to 10000) and whitelists the operator in the factory (isOperator = true).
formats.shown: "Create Operator" with the owner, name, operator fee %, maximum fee %, recipients and percentages.

findings.title: createOperator shows recipients and percentages as two separate lists the signer must pair by position.
findings.evidence: descriptor fields '#._recipients.[]' 'Recipients' and '#._percents.[]' 'Percentages' are separate parallel arrays; Operator._setRecipients pairs _recipients[i] with _percentsBps[i].
findings.fix: Render each recipient with its percentage, for example in an interpolatedIntent or with labels that state the pairing, once the runners support it.

effects: Requires a whitelisted operator. Deploys a deterministic Splitter clone (salt = operator, msg.sender, salt).
Calls Splitter.init(operator, msg.sender), so the signer becomes the splitter's owner and the operator becomes its commission taker. The operator's fee rate is read from storage.
Moves no assets and takes no native value (not payable).
formats.shown: "Create Splitter" with the operator address and a raw salt.

findings.title: createSplitter does not say that the operator's fee, read from storage, will be cut from funds sent to the splitter.
findings.evidence: Factory._createSplitter: newSplitter.init(operator, msg.sender); Operator.operatorFee is held in the Operator's storage, not in the calldata.
findings.fix: Nothing to change in the descriptor. A label like 'Fee operator' on the Operator field would help.

findings.title: createSplitter shows the salt as raw hex. It only seeds the clone address.
findings.evidence: descriptor field '#.salt' 'Salt' format raw; Factory._createSplitter uses it only in keccak256(abi.encodePacked(operator, msg.sender, salt)).
findings.fix: Set the Salt field to visible: optional or never.

formats.key: createSplitterAndCall(address operator, bytes32 salt, address callAddress, bytes data)
effects: Creates a Splitter clone owned by the signer, linked to the whitelisted operator (same as createSplitter).

Forwards all of msg.value as ETH to callAddress, with arbitrary calldata `data` called from the factory. In case 0 this sent 33.2 ETH to the Kiln staking contract and on to the beacon deposit contract.
Reverts the whole transaction if the sub-call fails.
formats.shown: "Create and Stake" with the operator, a raw salt and the call address, plus the nested staking call. That call shows the validator key, withdrawal credentials pointing to the signer and 33.2 ETH per validator.

findings.title: createSplitterAndCall is payable but has no top-level field for the total ETH sent (@.value).
findings.evidence: Factory.createSplitterAndCall: callAddress.call{value: msg.value}(data). The descriptor only passes '@.value' as amountPath to the nested calldata field. In case 0 the total of 33.2 ETH shows only as the inner 'Amount Per Validator'.
findings.fix: Add a field { path: '@.value', label: 'Amount', format: 'amount' } so the total ETH leaving is always shown, whatever the callee descriptor renders.

findings.title: createSplitterAndCall's intent 'Create and Stake' is fixed, but the call can go to any address with any data.
findings.evidence: Factory.createSplitterAndCall accepts any callAddress and data. Descriptor intent: "Create and Stake".
findings.fix: Use a neutral intent such as 'Create splitter and call', or an interpolatedIntent naming the call address and value.

findings.title: createSplitterAndCall does not say that the new splitter, owned by the signer, routes an operator fee read from storage.
findings.evidence: Factory._createSplitter: newSplitter.init(operator, msg.sender). Operator.operatorFee is in storage. In case 0 the withdrawal credentials point to the signer, not to the splitter.
findings.fix: Nothing to change in the descriptor.

findings.title: createSplitterAndCall shows the salt as raw hex. It has no meaning for the signer.
findings.evidence: descriptor field '#.salt' 'Salt' format raw, with no visible key.
findings.fix: Set visible: optional or never on Salt.

cases.notes: The only signer effect is 33.2 ETH out. The nested screen shows 33.2 ETH per validator with one validator, so the amount matches. The reader understood the stake correctly but was unsure whether the per-validator amount was the total.

effects: Only the factory owner can call it. It sets pendingOwner = newOwner (Ownable2Step).
Ownership of the factory, which includes the right to create operators, moves only after newOwner calls acceptOwnership.
formats.shown: "Start owner transfer" with the new owner address.

couldNotCheck: Splitter.sol (the IMPLEMENTATION cloned by createSplitter and createSplitterAndCall) is not in the directory. Its init(operator, owner) runs in the transaction, and it decides the owner's rights and the fee cut on funds sent to the splitter.
